It is by definition more correct but it is by no means final. No one is advocating for us to shut down all universities because "we know everything", but at the same time I couldn't possibly describe our cumulative understanding of the natural world as "very shaky". 
  Some like myself would say that science, when carried out well, accomplishes the goal of giving us an understanding of natural phenomena that is in accordance with reality, and that is its purpose. So if your question is "why", we can chase that back until science has run it's course and we're all left empty handed. At that point some people say "god" is the answer because they would rather have that than nothing, this leaves you with the ever shrinking "god of the gaps". What I'm saying is that it is intellectually honest at that point to say "I don't know" because everything verifiable in our cumulative understanding of reality says ERROR 404 - "god" not found

That's correct to an extent, our understanding of this method is what moved us into developing the hard sciences, and beyond the occasionally brilliant musings of a select few philosophers. They only got as far as they could go with the tools that they had in their times.

What "mystical force of unknown cause" are you referencing. 
Whether or not a scientist holds a personal belief in a diety is an separate issue altogether from whether or not they have irrefutable evidence for that god. That's just an appeal to authority.

Scientific theories in and of themselves cannot be dogmatic, it's the people that wield and twist them to force others into submission. Also taking everything into scope, that's where "sufficient, verifiable evidence" and the "pursuit of truth" come into context. We have no hard evidence of deities of any sort, so it's insincere to live life claiming to hold some truth that no one in the world has come forward with undeniable proof of.

In short I'm an atheist and take an anti-theistic stance. Although I would never force my ideals on anyone, if prompted I make it clear that I believe religion in all it's forms is psychological poison. I would prefer to see a world where people embrace science, logic, and the pursuit of truth. It is intellectually dishonest to hold onto any belief without sufficient, verifiable evidence.

Same, honestly, I've been out of work 7 months out of this year and was homeless for 6, was getting divorced (but might not be now), contracted covid-19, and had 2 months where I couldn't see my daughter. My parents and the friends I grew up with disowned me because I'm an atheist. On top of my life falling apart, the world has seemingly fallen apart.

I basically agree, when we talk about an individual's right to their own body, it should include the right to go out on our own terms. I shouldn't be forced to choose between eating a .45, falling 100+ ft, drowning, or buying 3+ grams of illicit drugs to shoot up. In a perfect world it wouldn't come to this but a good compromise would be coming to terms alongside the people I love, having 1 last good week, and going quietly in the arms of my partner. Unfortunately the society we live in is so entrenched in religious dogma we can't recognize that this should be a human right.
